summary: New SCV and Kähler geometry design with an actual-function complex-differential, complex-Hessian and boundary Levi foundation. The prefix fixes derivative normalizations, proves scalar and holomorphic chain rules, and distinguishes ambient Hessian positivity from tangent boundary positivity. Its defining-function comparison is exactly the C2 multiplier case; the general C2 ratio trap and upper-semicontinuous psh theory remain explicit proof obligations. Existing real Hessians, Laplacians, one-variable harmonic theory, analytic sheaf machinery, Sobolev carriers and linear Hodge structures are reused. The global Stein, Kähler and positivity/embedding branches have precise hypotheses and remaining source work, not completion claims.

nodes.title: The complex differential
nodes.statement: Construct the complex-linear functional partial u_x(v)=(D_R u_x(v)-i D_R u_x(iv))/2 from the actual first derivative. Reuse the complex linear-map carrier.
hypotheses: E is a complex normed space with its compatible real scalar restriction; u is an actual real-valued function.
proofSteps: Real linearity gives additivity. Write a=r+i s; expand a v=r v+s iv and i(a v)=-s v+r iv. The formula becomes a times partial u_x(v), proving complex linearity.
The construction uses total fderiv. Geometric uses retain differentiability hypotheses; fallback values at nonsmooth functions are not evidence of regularity.
acceptance: For u=Re z the result is v/2, not v or its conjugate.

sources.locator: Section 2.3, complex derivatives and Definition 2.3.5, pp.62–66
sources.match: Actual-function refinement of the stated complex-derivative convention.

nodes.title: The complex tangent kernel
nodes.statement: A vector lies in ker(partial u_x) exactly when Du_x(v)=0 and Du_x(iv)=0. On a regular level hypersurface this is the real tangent intersected with its i-translate.
hypotheses: The derivative and kernel are those of the actual real-valued function on the complex normed space.
proofSteps: Equality to zero in C is equality of both real components. Use the evaluation formula and invertibility of two.
The algebraic statement does not construct a level manifold. Its tangent interpretation uses the separate implicit-function interface.
acceptance: A real tangent vector need not be complex tangent; both equations matter.

sources.locator: Section 2.3, complex tangent and Definition 2.3.5, pp.62–66

nodes.title: Diagonal of the complex Hessian
nodes.statement: Define L_u(x;v)=(D_R^2 u_x(v,v)+D_R^2 u_x(iv,iv))/4 using the existing bilinearIteratedFDerivTwo. This is a real diagonal, not a new Hermitian carrier or boundary restriction.
hypotheses: E is a complex normed space with compatible real structure, and u is real-valued.
proofSteps: Evaluate the existing real bilinear second derivative at the two pairs and divide by four.
The mixed-derivative comparison proves agreement with the complex Hessian for C2 functions. Positivity is used with that regularity, not as the definition of general psh functions.
acceptance: For |z|^2 the result is |v|^2, whereas the real Hessian diagonal is 2|v|^2.

sources.locator: Section 2.3, complex Hessian and Definition 2.3.5, pp.62–66
sources.match: Explicit actual-function real-diagonal presentation, with the mixed-derivative comparison proved separately.

uses.how: The C2 psh criterion uses this diagonal after the line-subharmonic comparison.

nodes.title: Real-derivative formula for the complex Hessian
nodes.statement: L_u(x;v) is one fourth of the sum of fderiv R (fderiv R u) at (v,v) and (iv,iv).
hypotheses: The operators are the actual derivatives on the compatible real/complex normed space.
proofSteps: Unfold bilinearIteratedFDerivTwo and the diagonal definition.
acceptance: No arbitrary second jet or separate Hessian matrix is introduced.

sources.match: Evaluation of the actual derivative-based definition.

nodes.title: Complex scaling of the Hessian diagonal
nodes.statement: For a complex scalar a and C2 u, L_u(x;a v)=|a|^2 L_u(x;v).
hypotheses: u is C2 over R at x; E has compatible real and complex normed-space structures.
proofSteps: Write a=r+i s. Expand both real bilinear evaluations. The mixed terms cancel between a v and i a v, leaving the coefficient r^2+s^2=|a|^2.
acceptance: Multiplication by i preserves the diagonal; multiplication by zero kills it.

sources.match: The scaling is proved on the actual real-diagonal presentation.

nodes.title: Addition of complex Hessians
nodes.statement: For C2 real u,w near x, L_(u+w)(x;v)=L_u(x;v)+L_w(x;v).
hypotheses: Both functions are C2 over R at x on the compatible real/complex space.
proofSteps: Differentiate the sum twice; C2 supplies neighborhood differentiability for both steps. Evaluate at v and iv and add the two resulting identities.
acceptance: This is not unconditional linearity of the total derivative on arbitrary nonsmooth functions.

sources.match: Actual-function derivative calculation under the stated C2 hypotheses.

nodes.title: Comparison with the mixed complex derivative
nodes.statement: For C2 u, the complex cast of L_u(x;v) equals one half of the sum of D_R(y mapped to partial u_y(v))_x(v) and i times its value on iv. This is the barpartial derivative of the fixed-direction partial derivative.
hypotheses: u is C2 over R at x; all derivatives are of the displayed actual functions.
proofSteps: Differentiate complexDifferential_apply with v fixed, using bounded bilinear evaluation. The result is one fourth of H(v,v)+H(iv,iv)+i(H(iv,v)-H(v,iv)).
The pinned C2 symmetry theorem cancels the imaginary cross terms. The remaining expression is the defined real diagonal.
acceptance: Agreement is with a genuine mixed derivative, not an unrelated formal Hessian.

sources.locator: Section 2.3, complex second derivatives and Hessian, pp.62–66
sources.match: Explicit proof that the chosen real-diagonal presentation equals the source mixed derivative.

nodes.title: Laplacian on an affine complex line
nodes.statement: For C2 u near x and any v, the actual Laplacian at zero of z mapped to u(x+z v) equals 4 L_u(x;v).
hypotheses: u is C2 over R at x; the affine line uses complex scalar multiplication on E.
proofSteps: Apply the real chain rule twice to the affine line. Its derivative sends 1 to v and i to iv; its second derivative is zero.
Use the pinned complex-plane Laplacian and bilinear/iterated-derivative comparison. Its two summands are precisely those of the complex-Hessian diagonal.
acceptance: The constant line gives zero. For u=|z|^2 on C the factor is four.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.4.9 and its line-restriction calculation, printed p.85
sources.match: The differential calculation in the source criterion is instantiated to the existing Laplacian, without assuming the missing general subharmonic theory.

nodes.title: Product rule for complex Hessians
nodes.statement: For real C2 u,w, L_(u w)=u L_w+w L_u+2 Re(partial u(v) conjugate(partial w(v))) at x.
hypotheses: Both functions are C2 over R at x.
proofSteps: Differentiate the real product rule twice. The diagonal cross term is 2 Du(v)Dw(v), with its companion in iv.
Divide the sum by four and use the two components of the complex differential to identify the real product term.
acceptance: The cross term can be nonzero even when both separate Hessians vanish.

sources.match: Authored expansion of the actual derivative product rule, not a separately numbered source theorem.

nodes.title: Real scalar chain rule
nodes.statement: For real C2 chi at u(x) and C2 u at x, L_(chi composed with u)=chi_prime(u(x)) L_u+chi_second(u(x)) |partial u(v)|^2.
hypotheses: Both C2 hypotheses refer to the actual functions at the indicated points.
proofSteps: Differentiate the first real chain rule with the scalar/bilinear product rule. The second derivative is chi_prime H_u(v,w)+chi_second Du(v)Du(w).
Evaluate on (v,v) and (iv,iv), add and divide by four. The squared first derivatives divided by four are |partial u(v)|^2.
acceptance: For chi(t)=t^2 the coefficient of the squared complex differential is two.

sources.locator: Section 2.4, Proposition 2.4.9 and scalar convex composition in Exercise 2.4.15
sources.match: The C2 chain formula is explicitly proved here; citation to the exercise is not claimed as its solution.

nodes.title: Nonnegative Hessian under convex composition
nodes.statement: If L_u(x;v) is nonnegative for all v and chi_prime(u(x)),chi_second(u(x)) are nonnegative, then the diagonal of chi composed with u is nonnegative in all directions.
hypotheses: The C2 hypotheses of the scalar chain rule hold.
proofSteps: Apply the scalar chain formula and nonnegativity of a squared complex norm. Both summands are nonnegative.
acceptance: This is a smooth differential assertion, not the definition or full composition theorem for upper-semicontinuous psh functions.

sources.match: The actual smooth calculation supplies this implication; nonsmooth regularization remains separate.

nodes.title: Complex-line trace of a holomorphic second derivative
nodes.statement: For an actual complex-C2 map f:E->F, D_R^2 f_x(v,v)+D_R^2 f_x(iv,iv)=0.
hypotheses: E,F have compatible complex and real normed-space structures; f is C2 over C at x.
proofSteps: Use the pinned equality of the real derivative and the restricted complex derivative on a neighborhood of differentiability. Differentiate it and restrict the actual second derivative as well.
Complex bilinearity makes evaluation at iv,iv multiply the value at v,v by i^2=-1. This concerns the actual complex map, not a merely real-smooth map with an unrelated jet.
acceptance: For z mapped to z^2 the two individual second derivatives are nonzero but their sum is zero.

sources.match: Explicit restricted-scalar calculation for the holomorphic map, needed by the second chain rule.

nodes.title: Pullback of the complex Hessian
nodes.statement: For complex-C2 f:E->F and real-C2 u near f(x), L_(u composed with f)(x;v)=L_u(f(x);D_C f_x(v)).
hypotheses: f is C2 over C at x; u is C2 over R at f(x), on the compatible scalar structures.
proofSteps: Differentiate the real chain rule twice. It has terms H_u(Df v,Df w) and Du(D_R^2 f(v,w)), using the bounded bilinear derivative rule.
The first derivative is complex-linear after scalar restriction, so its two directional terms form the desired Hessian. The two second-derivative terms sum to zero by holomorphic-second-trace.
acceptance: Real smoothness is insufficient. Strict positivity needs injectivity of Df; f(z)=z^2 loses it at zero.

sources.match: The pullback formula is proved through the actual second chain rule, not assumed for arbitrary jets.

nodes.title: Pullback of the complex differential
nodes.statement: For real-differentiable u at f(x) and complex-differentiable f at x, partial(u composed with f)_x is partial u_f(x) composed with D_C f_x as actual complex linear maps.
hypotheses: Only the two stated first derivatives are needed.
proofSteps: Apply the real first chain rule and scalar restriction. Use Df(iv)=i Df(v) in the two evaluation terms. Linear-map extensionality proves equality.
acceptance: Invertibility of the holomorphic map is not assumed.

sources.match: Actual first-order chain rule in the chosen normalization.

nodes.title: Vanishing on real parts of holomorphic functions
nodes.statement: The diagonal complex Hessian of Re f vanishes for an actual complex-C2 scalar function f.
hypotheses: f:E->C is C2 over C at x.
proofSteps: Real part is a continuous real linear map. Differentiate its composite twice and apply it to holomorphic-second-trace.
acceptance: Re(z^2) has vanishing complex Hessian but an indefinite real Hessian and is not real convex.

sources.match: The smooth vanishing consequence is proved directly, without redefining general pluriharmonicity.

nodes.title: Complex Hessian of the squared modulus
nodes.statement: For the existing Complex.normSq on C, L_u(x;v)=|v|^2.
hypotheses: The scalar domain is C with its standard real structure.
proofSteps: Expand |z|^2=(Re z)^2+(Im z)^2 and differentiate twice. Its real Hessian is twice the Euclidean pairing. Insert the two directions in the defining average.
acceptance: The value is independent of x and pins the factor four.

sources.match: Actual polynomial calculation in the chosen normalization.

nodes.title: Complex Hessian of a squared holomorphic function
nodes.statement: For a complex-C2 scalar f, L_(|f|^2)(x;v)=|D_C f_x(v)|^2.
hypotheses: f:E->C is C2 over C at x.
proofSteps: Apply holomorphic-hessian-pullback to the existing squared-modulus function and substitute squared-norm-hessian.
acceptance: For f(z)=z^2 the value at zero is zero. Nonconstant holomorphy does not imply strict positivity.

sources.locator: Section 2.4, smooth Hessian criterion and holomorphic examples
sources.match: An explicit consequence of the two proved actual-function formulas.

nodes.title: Real derivative of a rescaled defining function
nodes.statement: At rho(x)=0, D_R(h rho)_x=h(x) D_R rho_x.
hypotheses: rho,h are real-differentiable at x on the complex normed space.
proofSteps: Apply the actual product derivative rule. Its term multiplied by rho(x) vanishes.
acceptance: This first-order identity needs no second derivative of the multiplier.

sources.match: Explicit first-order multiplier calculation under the stated regularity.

nodes.title: Complex differential of a rescaled defining function
nodes.statement: At rho(x)=0, partial(h rho)_x=h(x) partial rho_x as actual complex-linear maps.
hypotheses: rho,h are real-differentiable at x.
proofSteps: Insert the real-derivative multiplier identity into both terms of the complex differential. The real scalar h(x) factors through the complex expression.
acceptance: This concerns the full first differential at the zero level.

sources.match: Actual complex-linear version of the first-order identity.

nodes.title: Equality of complex tangent kernels
nodes.statement: At rho(x)=0 with h(x) nonzero, partial(h rho)_x and partial rho_x have the same existing kernel submodule.
hypotheses: rho,h are real-differentiable at x and the multiplier value is nonzero.
proofSteps: Their complex differentials differ by the nonzero scalar h(x). Invertibility of that scalar identifies their zero loci.
acceptance: A zero multiplier is excluded; no replacement tangent carrier is constructed.

sources.locator: I, Section 7.C, complex tangent before (7.10), p.58
sources.match: Exact kernel comparison for a nonzero multiplier.

nodes.title: Tangential Hessian under a smooth multiplier
nodes.statement: At rho(x)=0 and v in ker(partial rho_x), L_(h rho)(x;v)=h(x)L_rho(x;v).
hypotheses: Both rho and the GIVEN multiplier h are C2 over R at x.
proofSteps: Apply hessian-product. The term multiplied by rho(x) is zero, and the cross term is zero since partial rho_x(v)=0.
This is not an equality on all ambient directions. It does not infer a C2 multiplier from arbitrary C2 defining functions.
acceptance: A normal direction can acquire negative Hessian while the tangent form is unchanged.

sources.match: Only the explicit C2-multiplier case is proved here. Full intrinsic defining-function independence remains a separate regularity obligation.

nodes.title: Regularity after nonzero rescaling
nodes.statement: At rho(x)=0, h(x) nonzero and D_R rho_x nonzero imply D_R(h rho)_x nonzero.
hypotheses: Both factors are real-differentiable at x.
proofSteps: Use boundary-factor-real-derivative. Multiplication of a nonzero continuous real linear map by a nonzero real scalar is nonzero.
acceptance: The zero multiplier would destroy regularity and is excluded.

sources.match: Preserves the actual nonzero-derivative requirement.

nodes.title: Normalized boundary Levi diagonal
nodes.statement: Restrict the actual diagonal L_rho(x;v) to v in ker(partial rho_x), and divide by the operator norm of D_R rho_x. A nonzero-derivative witness is an explicit input. In Euclidean space the denominator equals the gradient norm used by Demailly.
hypotheses: E has compatible real/complex normed-space structures. Boundary applications additionally carry C2 regularity, rho(x)=0 and the negative-inside convention.
The ambient norm is fixed. Exact invariance under an arbitrary change of norm is not asserted.
proofSteps: Use the existing kernel subtype and the actual Hessian diagonal. A nonzero continuous linear derivative has positive operator norm, so divide by it.
The API records evaluation, equivalence of nonnegativity with the tangent diagonal, and independence from the regularity proof. No boundary manifold or full Hermitian carrier is postulated.
acceptance: A normal ambient vector is not an argument to this tangent form.

sources.locator: I, equation (7.10) and preceding tangent conventions, p.58
sources.match: The source gradient normalization is instantiated as operator-norm normalization on actual tangent vectors.

uses.how: The regular defining function supplies the scalar-normalized boundary diagonal.
Separates orientation-preserving rescaling from a change of inside.

api.name: TauCeti.ComplexGeometry.normalizedLevi_nonneg_iff
api.statement: Nonnegativity is equivalent to that of the unnormalized tangent diagonal.

api.name: TauCeti.ComplexGeometry.normalizedLevi_proof_independent
api.statement: A change of the nonzero-derivative proof changes no value.

tests.name: levi_sphere_value
tests.statement: For rho(z,w)=|z|^2+|w|^2-1 at (1,0), tangent (0,1) has value 1/2. The test supplies actual regularity and kernel witnesses.

tests.name: levi_halfspace_zero
tests.statement: For rho(z,w)=Re w at zero, tangent (1,0) has normalized value zero.

nodes.title: Evaluation of the normalized Levi diagonal
nodes.statement: The value is L_rho(x;v) divided by the operator norm of the actual derivative.
hypotheses: The derivative is nonzero; v belongs to the complex-differential kernel.
proofSteps: Unfold the restriction and scalar division in the construction.
acceptance: The input is a tangent subtype, not an arbitrary ambient vector.

sources.match: Evaluation of the chosen normalization.

nodes.title: Positivity and Levi normalization
nodes.statement: Nonnegativity of the normalized value is equivalent to nonnegativity of the complex-Hessian diagonal on the same tangent vector.
hypotheses: The actual real derivative is nonzero.
proofSteps: A nonzero continuous linear map has positive operator norm. Dividing by it preserves and reflects comparison with zero.
acceptance: A tangent positivity test is not replaced by positivity on all ambient directions.

sources.match: Order comparison with the source positive denominator.

nodes.title: Normalized Levi form and the choice of side
nodes.statement: For sigma=h rho at rho(x)=0, with rho,h C2 and h(x) nonzero, compare the normalized forms on the SAME ambient tangent vector using the kernel equality. Then Levi_norm_sigma=(h(x)/|h(x)|) Levi_norm_rho. A positive multiplier preserves the value; a negative one reverses the side.
hypotheses: rho,h are C2 at x, rho(x)=0, h(x) is nonzero and D_R rho_x is nonzero.
The suggested signature carries regularity and tangent witnesses for both forms; the earlier lemmas construct the second witnesses.
proofSteps: Tangential Hessians scale by h(x). The full first derivative scales by h(x), so its operator norm scales by |h(x)|.
Divide by the positive nonzero original norm. Kernel equality compares the same ambient vector.
Only the GIVEN C2 multiplier case is proved. Two arbitrary C2 defining functions need not have a C2 ratio, so the general same-boundary theorem requires the separate level-set argument.
acceptance: The sphere and its negative defining function have opposite values. A positive varying multiplier preserves the tangent normalized value.

sources.match: Explicit smooth-multiplier proof with the exact regularity restriction. It is not claimed to complete the broader intrinsic comparison.

nodes.title: The normal correction to a defining Hessian
nodes.statement: At rho(x)=0, replacing rho by rho+a rho^2 changes the full diagonal by 2a |partial rho_x(v)|^2. It leaves the tangent diagonal unchanged, not the ambient normal diagonal.
hypotheses: rho is C2 at x and a is real.
proofSteps: Apply the scalar chain rule to chi(t)=t+a t^2. At zero its first derivative is one and its second derivative is 2a.
acceptance: For rho=|z1|^2+|z2|^2-1, a=-1, at (1,0) the normal value is -1 and the tangent value +1. Since 1-rho is positive near the zero level, the defining functions have the same local inside.

sources.match: Authored actual-function test separating ambient and boundary Hessians; no source error is alleged.
